extracted.intended_audience: mineralogists, scientists, and students (members/readers of AAAS and Popular Science Monthly); practitioners and institutions involved in collecting, describing, and publishing mineralogical work
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical expectations for conducting, reporting, describing, and curating mineralogical research and collections (19th-century American context) — covering specimen submission, field reporting detail, descriptive rigor, textbooks, and publication/access practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / objective of investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Investigation of the Mineral and Fossil Bodies which compose the Fabric of the Globe, and more especially for the Natural and Chemical History of the Minerals and Fossils of the United States."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should aim at the natural and chemical history of minerals and fossils in the United States — research framed around these comprehensive objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field reporting details for mineral occurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: The society solicited communications "especially on the following," e.g.: 1. Concerning the stones suitable to be manufactured into gun-flints: where are they found? and in what quantity? 2. Concerning native orimstone or sulphur or the waters or minerals whence it may be extracted? 3. Concerning saltpeter: where (if at all) found native? or the soils which produce it in the United States? 4. Concerning mines and ores of lead: in what places? the situation? how wide the vein? in what kind of rock it is bedded?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field reports should include precise locality, quantity/extent, geological setting (rock type, vein width), and source information especially when resource/utility is involved. Practical, application-oriented details were valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen submission and retention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Specimens of ores, metals, coals, spars, gypsums, crystals, petrifactions, stones, earths, slates, clays, chalks, limestones, marbles, and every fossil substance ... will be examined and analyzed without cost, sufficient pieces, with the owner's leave, being reserved for placing in the society's collection."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting material for study, provide specimens sufficient for analysis and for retention in reference collections; societies/institutions expect to keep representative portions (with owner permission) to build public/reference cabinets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of mineral collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections brought to New York and elsewhere were made "fully accessible to all interested in seeing them," and their public exhibition "contributed ... to excite in the public an active interest in the science of mineralogy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curated collections should be made accessible to students, researchers, and the public to stimulate education and further research; open exhibition is a recognised mechanism to advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook standards for mineralogy
rubrics_metrics.description: There was a pressing want for a work which "should include the modern discoveries, and one also which should gather up the scattered facts already published in regard to American minerals" — a "thorough, systematic, and American treatise ... well suited to all classes of students."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational treatises should be up-to-date (include modern discoveries), comprehensive (gather scattered facts), systematic, adapted to local (American) material, and accessible to a broad student audience (including considerations of scope and affordability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and clearness in mineral descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: "These species remain to-day essentially as he described, and his papers may well be studied by mineralogists now as models of accuracy and clearness of statement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species descriptions and published papers should aim for high accuracy and clear, unambiguous statement; exemplary descriptions serve as models for future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigor in investigations (eyewitness and laboratory diligence)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the meteorite investigation: "The diligence employed in obtaining all the facts possible from eye-witnesses of the occurrence, and the care and skill shown in the chemical and mineralogical examination of the meteorite, made this paper one of the most remarkable memoirs of the time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field investigations should combine thorough collection of eyewitness/observational data with careful, skillful laboratory chemical and mineralogical analyses; both observational diligence and analytical rigor are required for high-quality studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for claiming new mineral species
rubrics_metrics.description: Of nearly three hundred supposed new American minerals: "Of these, perhaps one quarter are new to science, and the remainder have either been proved to be identical with species already described, or their characters are so imperfectly given that further investigation is needed to ascertain what they are."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of novelty must be supported by complete, well-documented characters; insufficient description or inadequate comparison invites synonymy with known species and necessitates further investigation before recognition as new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for reference collections for identification
rubrics_metrics.description: "It was necessary to have known minerals for study and comparison in order properly to determine those obtained by exploration here."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining reference collections (comparative specimens) is essential for accurate identification and determination of newly collected material; comparisons to known material are a fundamental part of taxonomic/mineral identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for recognition and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Colonel Gibbs "offered prizes for superiority of attainments in mineralogical knowledge and for services rendered to the science by useful discoveries and observations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition (prizes) should be awarded for demonstrable attainment in knowledge and for concrete contributions such as useful discoveries and observations — emphasizing both competence and practical impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and expectation of formal surveys and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: State surveys "published independent volumes on the mineralogy of their respective States, and these surveys have been a powerful auxiliary in extending our knowledge of the occurrence of minerals on this continent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive governmental or institutional surveys and their formal publications are expected to document mineral occurrences systematically and serve as authoritative references for the field; such publications are a standard mechanism for advancing and disseminating knowledge.
